title: What KeyGuard is
narration: This is KeyGuard, our submission for Track 4, Trust but Verify. It keeps files and messages safe when an identity key is lost, replaced or abused. All the cryptography is post-quantum, from OpenSSL 3.5: ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA. Keys are generated at runtime, and there is no AI or machine learning anywhere.

title: Start the authority
narration: We start the authority. It stores policy, the protected data and a signed audit log in one atomic SQLite transaction, with a write-ahead log and full sync. A crash can never leave a half-applied change, and we test that with real process kills.

title: Signed read (ML-DSA-65)
narration: The owner reads their file. Every network request is signed with ML-DSA-65. The signature covers the authority, the destination node, the key's epoch, a one-time nonce and an expiry. So a captured request can't be replayed, sent to another node, or used after the key changes.

title: Revoke the stolen device
narration: Now the owner's laptop is stolen, so the operator revokes the key. The answer doesn't just say done. It reports the moment the revocation is guaranteed on every read node, based on the longest lease still outstanding. Across one hundred revocations on five replicas, the ninety-ninth percentile was one point one seconds.

title: Stolen key is rejected
narration: The thief tries the stolen key. It's rejected, and it stays rejected after a restart and on every node.

title: The system detects the attack on itself
narration: KeyGuard also detects the attack on itself. The rejected attempt became a signed security alert that names the identity, the exact key, the service and the audit event. As a response, that identity's dashboard sessions and pending message keys are cancelled. Alerts are capped per identity per minute, so a thief can't flood the log.

title: Merkle tree head, ML-DSA + SLH-DSA
narration: The audit log is tamper-evident twice over: a SHA-384 hash chain and an RFC 9162 Merkle tree. Every audit answer can carry an inclusion proof, and the tree head is signed with both ML-DSA and SLH-DSA, so its integrity doesn't rest on a single signature scheme.

title: Detection with MITRE ATT&CK
narration: Detection combines rules with a graph: role changes without approval, access right after an unexplained role change, and lateral movement across services, including credential hopping between identities. Every alert names the identity, the events and the MITRE ATT&CK technique. On the organizer's practice set it finds five out of five with zero false alerts. On our two independently built holdouts, F1 is 0.90 and 0.96, and we report false alerts per thousand benign events and the median time to alert.

title: Committed evidence
narration: Every number we claim comes from committed evidence. One hundred and four out of one hundred and four tests pass offline on both ARM64 and AMD64, along with the organizer's validator and an independent post-quantum interop check. Messages use a hybrid X25519 plus ML-KEM key exchange, so they stay confidential if either primitive breaks.

title: Stated limits
narration: We state our limits. There's no Double Ratchet and no session resumption. A replica can honour an old lease for under a second, and we report exactly when. Lateral movement slower than thirty minutes is missed. The repository builds from the README on a clean machine. Thank you.
